newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam's eldest son Uday undergoes operation.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's eldest son Uday undergoes operation.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday had a successful operation on his left leg and said he expected to be on his feet again "in a few days or a few weeks".
Uday's comments were broadcast on his Shabab (youth) television channel on Tuesday.
"With God's help, on Sunday at noon a group of foreign doctors performed surgery on me," Uday said while lying in his hospital bed in Baghdad.
Uday was reported to have been shot and wounded by unidentified gunmen on December 12 as he was driving in Baghdad's wealthy district of al-Mansour.
Speaking in Arabic Uday said: "Praise be to God, the operation was successful and I am now on my way to a full recovery. God willing, in a few days or weeks I will be able to walk on my feet again."

"There is a possibility that he will go back 100 per cent as he was before," said Hassan al-Khudeiri, the Iraqi doctor who performed the operation along with other foreign doctors that Uday did not identify.
"They were not French doctors, they came from one of the friendly countries, and they were assisted by Iraqi doctors," Uday said.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee, owns the most influential newspaper Babel and runs the popular Shabab television channel.
"If God permits, I will be able to practice physical sport in six months while other tasks within our duties will be from two to three months," he said.
Dr al-Khudeiri said: "this is the last operation and I think he does not need any more."
Uday said he had been hit in both his legs. He has recovered from an operation on his right leg in January. He was also severely wounded in the left leg, which suffered a double fracture.
"The major problem at the moment is in my left leg. I have what they call a compound fracture," he said.
A few days after the assassination attempt, Uday blamed Iran for the attack. Officials from Tehran have denied the charge.
